title: Multimodal model predicts delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD
summary: In 3,416 patients at two hospitals, YOLOv11m-seg segmented post-ESD mucosal defects, ResNet50 produced an image score (E-Score), and this was fused with clinical features in an XGBoost model (PrismDB). Delayed bleeding occurred in 8.06% (development) and 8.31% (external) of patients. AUC was 0.804 in development and 0.788 (95% CI 0.724 to 0.850) in the external cohort of 638 patients, with 79.25% sensitivity and 97.79% negative predictive value. Low-risk classification did not exclude bleeding, calibration was not evaluated externally, and benefit of model-guided care is unproven.
ai_technology: YOLOv11m-seg segmentation, ResNet50 image score and XGBoost (PrismDB) fusion model
organization: Soochow University; Changshu No.1 People's Hospital

evidence.tested: External validation cohort of 638 patients after development in 2,778; AUC 0.788.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; external calibration untested; safety of model-guided care not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep networks scored endoscopic images of the wound and a boosted model combined that score with clinical data.
